options.text: A cloud machine that hosts the Claude model
A program that exposes tools and resources through a standard protocol, so AI clients like Claude Code can use them
A faster alternative to the Bash tool
A database Anthropic maintains of approved prompts

questions.explanation: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the USB of AI integrations: build a server once — say for Postgres or a browser — and any MCP client can plug into it.

questions.prompt: What problem does a STANDARD protocol solve here?

options.text: It makes models generate text faster
Without it, every AI app would need a custom integration for every external tool — MCP means one server works with every client
It removes the need for permissions

questions.explanation: N apps x M tools becomes N + M: tool builders write one MCP server; app builders write one MCP client. Same reason USB beat proprietary connectors.

questions.prompt: After you add a Postgres MCP server to Claude Code, how does Claude use it?

options.text: The server's tools (e.g., a query tool) join Claude's toolkit and are called through the same agent loop and permission system as built-in tools
Claude gains raw shell access to the database machine
The entire database is loaded into the context window
Claude emails queries to the server's maintainer

questions.explanation: MCP tools are just more tools: the model requests a call, the server executes, results come back into context — with permissions applying exactly as they do to Bash or Edit.

questions.prompt: Which are sensible cautions with MCP servers? (select all that apply)

options.text: Only install servers from sources you trust — they run real code with real access
Give servers the least credentials that work, e.g., a read-only database user
Connect every server you can find, to maximize capability
Remember that data returned by tools (web pages, tickets) can contain injected instructions

questions.explanation: MCP extends both capability and attack surface. Least privilege, trusted sources, and injection awareness apply. And every connected server's tool definitions spend context — connect what you need (c is the anti-pattern).
